newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower as hedging cited.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower as hedging cited.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on spillover weakness from other wheat markets, and traders noted heavy late selling in the May contract.

March was pressured by hedge selling throughout the session. Traders said that cold weather-related delays in grain movement should ease as temperatures were expected to be milder this week in the northern Plains.

U.S. wheat markets weakened after the Australian Wheat Board revised upward its estimate for Australian wheat production. Wheat also saw spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which eased in response to rains in Brazil.
MGE spring wheat settled 1-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with March down five cents at $3.80-1/4.

LFG sold two million May bushels, much of it coming late in the session. Traders said they did not know whether the business was related to commercial or commission house dealings. Atwood-Peavey bear-spread 2.3 million May/March bushels, which traders said was linked to the expected increase in country movement.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to three cents per cwt lower, with March unchanged at $6.70.
